paper_title: Approximate Monotone Local Search for Weighted Problems
classifications: Theory of computation → Approximation algorithms analysis
statement: that minimizes the weight and satisfies a certain fixed property. What is the analogue of brute-force in this setting? Can bi-objective parameterized approximation algorithms for weighted monotone subset minimization problems be used to design faster (than brute force) exponential approximation algorithms in this restrictive setting? What happens if we extend this setting to a bi-criteria optimization setting?
context: This leads to the following natural question. Consider more restrictive weighted monotone subset minimization problems where given a universe U on n vertices, a weight function w on the elements of the universe, the goal is to find a subset of the universe of size at most k that minimizes the weight and satisfies a certain fixed property. What is the analogue of brute-force in this setting? Can bi-objective parameterized approximation algorithms for weighted monotone subset minimization problems be used to design faster (than brute force) exponential approximation algorithms in this restrictive setting? What happens if we extend this setting to a bi-criteria optimization setting?
